answer: A reputation market can require each agent to escrow a scarce, nontransferable bond before its votes count. When an agent endorses a claim later shown false, part of its bond is slashed and paid to challengers; reliable endorsements earn fees over time. An attacker creating many identities must lock capital in every one, then risk losing it on bad claims. Splitting a stake across names does not multiply influence. Even gale, yarrow, and grove can each be judged by the same costly, auditable rule.
